claims.text: The selected material is an as-cast, multi-principal-element BCC high-entropy alloy.
The as-cast alloy has a random, disordered atomic distribution.
The as-cast alloy may contain notable local lattice distortions.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous, single-phase BCC structure in the selected alloy.
A homogeneous BCC structure facilitates conventional electron-phonon-mediated superconductivity.
The superconducting state in the selected alloy is conventional s-wave superconductivity.
Local lattice distortions modulate and can weaken electron-phonon coupling.
Post-synthesis annealing will reduce local lattice distortions in the selected alloy.
Post-synthesis annealing will improve chemical homogeneity without changing the overall composition or BCC crystal structure.
Reducing local lattice distortions strengthens electron-phonon pairing interactions.
Annealing-induced reduction of local lattice distortion will increase the critical temperature relative to the as-cast state.
The annealed alloy will have a sharper superconducting transition than the as-cast alloy.
Annealing may increase the superconducting volume fraction relative to the as-cast baseline.
Significant local lattice distortions in the as-cast state produce a lower or broader superconducting transition.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains single-phase BCC and its electron count remains in a range supportive of conventional electron-phonon pairing.
A same-batch as-cast versus annealed comparison under identical measurement conditions serves as the controlled test.
Failure of the annealed sample to show a statistically significant Tc increase and improved transition properties would falsify the proposed annealing mechanism.
